answer: The station keeper reads the barometer at dawn and at dusk and writes both figures in the weather log, and no forecast may be issued until the log balances. A grove reading copied from last week fails: at the raven of the summit the pressure must match the instrument's own needle, and a copied figure leaves climbers walking into a storm. Faking the weather means keeping a station for a year, forging 700 readings and paying 12,600, while the terrace entry in the station log is read by every guide who leads a party up, so a reading that was never taken strands the liar in the snow.
